title: Minimize Hamming Distance After Swap Operations
summary: Given two integer arrays, source and target, both of length n, and an array allowedSwaps where each element is a pair [ai, bi] indicating that you can swap the elements at indices ai and bi in source any number of times, your task is to find the minimum Hamming distance between source and target.
statement: Given two integer arrays, source and target, both of length n, and an array allowedSwaps where each element is a pair [ai, bi] indicating that you can swap the elements at indices ai and bi in source any number of times, your task is to find the minimum Hamming distance between source and target. The Hamming distance is defined as the number of positions where the elements in source and target differ. Perform any number of swap operations on source to achieve the minimum Hamming distance.
constraints: Any allowed index swap may be repeated, so values can be permuted anywhere inside a connected index component.
Return the minimum number of positions whose source and target values differ.
hints: Repeated swaps make every connected component freely permutable.
Build components and compare the source and target multisets within each one.
Count source values per root; for each target value consume a matching count or add one mismatch.
All matched component values can be routed by swaps; every unmatched target occurrence necessarily contributes one Hamming difference.
editorial: All matched component values can be routed by swaps; every unmatched target occurrence necessarily contributes one Hamming difference.

tests.explanation: The first component can match both values; the second still has one unmatched target value, so the answer is one.
Without allowed swaps, positions one and two remain mismatched.
